newsitem.title: USA: Staples prepared to fight FTC in court.
newsitem.headline: Staples prepared to fight FTC in court.

text.p: Staples Inc chief executive Thomas Stemberg said there is better than a 50 percent chance the company will fight the Federal Trade Commission decision on its proposed merger with Office Depot Inc in court.

"If I were a betting man, I think it's highly likely that this matter will end up in litigation. Much higher than a 50 percent probability," Stemberg told reporters on a conference call from San Diego. He said the company is prepared to fight the decision against the merger, and a court of law would agree with Staples position.
"We feel very confident that there is strong merit to our position," he added. "I think it's a reasonable conclusion this is going to end up in court."
Stemberg said he was surprised with the decision and repeatedly accused the FTC of "flip-flopping" on the decision.

"The Commission once again flip-flopped as they have had a history of doing throughout our seven months in fantasyland with them and voted against this solution," he said. "We did exactly as they wanted us to do, at tremendous costs."
He added that he would have difficulty negotiating with the commission in the future.

He indicated that Staples would likely not try to restructure the proposed merger again, but added that he still believed the deal was in the best interests of the two companies, its shareholders and its customers.
"I'm hard-pressed to see why we would try to strike another agreement with them (the FTC)," he said.
Stemberg estimated that Staples and Office Depot spent at least $10 million to comply with the FTC, only to see the merger scuttled.
Both companies had a long history of cutting prices on products and Stemberg said he found it confusing that the FTC would now worry that the merger would result in higher prices.

The FTC decision also had a human dimension in that it disrupted the plans of many Staples and Office Depot employees. He met Friday in San Diego with the employees of nine Staples stores which were to be sold to rival OfficeMax Inc under terms of the merger.
